description: The caller can cancel a call in flight: HTTP aborts the request, gRPC cancels the call, messaging publishes a cancel event on the control channel, MCP closes the request stream (HTTP) or sends notifications/cancelled (stdio). The dispatcher's abort signal fires in the node.

cases.description: Cancel 100 ms into a 5 s call: the caller gets `cancelled` at once and the node's signal is aborted.
Cancelling a call that already replied changes nothing: the reply stands.
A call cancelled before the consumer takes it must not run at all (messaging: the cancel on the control channel is matched by id when the request is picked up).
A cancelled node never produces a normal reply with error `cancelled` on the caller side: the outcome is the transport error, so retries and "continue on fail" don't treat it as a node failure.
